recaps.title: Week 3 Recap: Slumlords Print 299, Hyper’s 281.5 Still an L, Divers Off the Bus
recaps.coldOpen: Week 3 in IDP country: a 299 kitty from a team that started 0-2 and already rode the Survivor bus, a 281.5 that still loses, and a former 2-0 Divers board that bottomed out at 144 and walked off the bus. Ryan Towner’s Slumlords beat Jacob Crisp’s Hyper in a street fight, then stayed alive on Last Ride while Gavin’s Dongers got eliminated for good. Mike Heff’s Goats are the league’s only 3-0. Chase’s TTAB took its first L. Luke’s Saltese finally blinked. Hero of the week: Slumlords at 299 (Gibbs 42 / Fannin 29 / Cook 27) with a Maye ceremonial 1, plus that Last Ride stay-alive. Goat of the week: Morningside’s 144 — and a format that turns Hyper’s 281.5 into heartbreak.
heroes: Slumlords 299 — Gibbs 42 / Fannin 29 / Cook 27; Maye 1 punchline; week kitty + Last Ride stay-alive
Hyper’s 281.5 — quality-loss club with Sadiq 34.5; league-high PF, still 1-2
Eddies’ first W — Bowers 41.5 / Warner 41 / G. Wilson 32
Newman’s skill stack — Juwan 30.5 / Golden 27 / Adams 26; ended Saltese’s perfect start
Purdy 44 + London 36 (Sub) — nuclear skill half that still lost to Pocket IDP
goats: Morningside 144 — off the bus; Achane 1 / JJ 5 / Price −1
Dongers 0-3 — Bijan 44 wasted; out of Last Ride for good
TTAB 192 — Allen’s 15; first L after the Week 1 lottery
Maye’s 1 — ceremonial QB on a kitty winner
Gadsden 0 / Waddle 6 / Kincaid 3.5 — quiet hours across three otherwise grown-up cards

matchups.blurb: Ryan Towner did not ask for a soft landing after Weeks 1–2 — he ordered a **299** kitty. The punchline writes itself: **Drake Maye scored 1**, and the board still nuked the week on **Jahmyr Gibbs (42), Harold Fannin (29), and James Cook (27)** while the IDP unit printed a league-bully **176**. Jacob Crisp’s Hyper put up a very real **281.5** — season-long PF leader vibes — with **Kenyon Sadiq’s 34.5** and **Kenneth Walker’s 23**, and still left empty-handed. Same movie as Week 2’s quality-loss club, just with a higher price of admission. Juice: 299 kitty; Gibbs/Fannin/Cook triad; Last Ride still breathing. Junk: Maye’s 1; 281.5 as a losing number; Hyper to 1-2 with the league’s highest PF.

Bill’s Eddies cashed their first W of 2026 the IDP way. **Brock Bowers dropped 41.5**, **Fred Warner matched him with 41**, and **Garrett Wilson added 32** while the defense choir (Leonard Williams 21 / Jordyn Brooks 21 / Evan Williams 20) finished the job at **263.5**. Gavin’s Dongers brought **Bijan Robinson’s 44**, **Joe Burrow’s 27**, and **Chris Olave’s 25** — a skill stack that should buy wins — and still finished **224** and **0-3**. Worse: on Last Ride math (Slumlords 299 vs Dongers 224), Gavin is out of the re-entry path for good. Juice: Bowers/Warner twin towers; Eddies off the schneid. Junk: Bijan’s 44 in a funeral; Dongers’ Last Ride eviction.

matchups.scoreline: Newman Lake Sleep Paralysis Demons 263.5, Saltese Slamm 235
matchups.blurb: Rymo’s Newman ended Luke’s undefeated run with a skill-board crime spree. **Juwan Johnson’s 30.5**, **Matthew Golden’s 27**, **Davante Adams’ 26**, and **Tee Higgins’ 21** stacked a **142.5** offense and a **263.5** final. Luke’s Saltese still got **Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s 40** and **Matthew Stafford’s 25** — JSN leads the league OMVP board at 126 YTD — and watched **Oronde Gadsden post a zero** while the rest of the flex room stayed quiet-adjacent. Rookie franchise, first scar. Juice: Newman’s WR/TE explosion; Luke’s first L. Junk: Gadsden’s 0; 235 as a respectable loss that still stings.

Kyle’s dual-era champ finally cashed a W after the 0-2 hole. Doubtpfizer closed **265** behind **CMC’s 23**, **Dak’s 20**, and an IDP unit that outworked the skill gap (**157** defense). Brian Aga’s Ultron brought real juice — **Michael Wilson 25, Ja’Marr Chase 24, Terry McLaurin 19** — and still left at **240** with **Terrance Ferguson’s 2** as the sour TE note. Not a collapse. Just the champ remembering how to win ugly. Juice: Doubtpfizer off the schneid; CMC being CMC. Junk: Ferguson’s 2; Ultron stuck at 1-2.

Kellen “the Host” Olson won the IDP math olympiad. Pocket’s offense managed a modest **98.5** — **CeeDee 26 / Goff 22 / McBride 22**, with **Waddle at 6** and **Kincaid at 3.5** after last week’s TE party — while the defense printed **158** and dragged the board to **256.5**. Nate’s Substation threw **Brock Purdy’s 44** and **Drake London’s 36** at the problem and still could not survive a **91**-point IDP floor. That’s the week’s thesis in one box: forty-four from your QB is not a win if the other guy’s linebackers clock in. Juice: Pocket to 2-1 on IDP bullying. Junk: Purdy 44 / London 36 in an L; Waddle’s quiet encore.

matchups.scoreline: Little Ass Boys 239.5, Towner Top Aga Bottom 192
matchups.blurb: Jesse’s LAB ended Chase’s perfect start. **Jaylen Warren (27), Jeremiyah Love (24), and Kyren Williams (23)** did adult RB things while the IDP unit added **135** for a **239.5** close. Chase’s TTAB — Week 1 kitty kings — bottomed to **192** with **Josh Allen managing 15** (two picks and a fumble in the box) and a defense that only found **90**. **Christian Watson’s 22** showed up; the rest of the 315 hangover did not. Juice: LAB’s RB triad; TTAB’s first scar. Junk: Allen’s 15; Shakir’s 1 on the winning side as a free punchline; 192 from a former nuclear stack.

matchups.scoreline: Valley Old Goats 219, Morningside Muff Divers 144
matchups.blurb: Heff’s Goats went to **3-0** the professional way: **George Kittle’s 32** and **Derrick Henry’s 24** over Tim’s Divers in a game that was never a game. Divers posted the league floor at **144** — **Devon Achane 1, Justin Jefferson 5, Jadarian Price −1** — and got Survivor-eliminated after opening 2-0. **Deebo’s 28** and **Lamar’s 24** were lighthouses in a fog. Off the bus. Juice: Goats alone at 3-0; Kittle’s 32. Junk: 144 league floor; Achane/JJ/Price crime scene; a 2-0 start erased in one Tuesday.

recaps.closer: Kitty to Slumlords. League floor — and the Survivor bus — to Morningside. Hyper cracked 281 and still lost. Heff alone at 3-0. Luke and Chase both took their first scars. Eddies and Doubtpfizer cashed first wins. Last Ride: Slumlords stay alive; Dongers are done. WWJDD: start your studs, fear IDP math, and don’t confuse a 280 with a win.

recaps.title: Week 2 Recap: Host Hits 322, Lloyd’s 66, Three Boards Over 250 Still Lose
recaps.coldOpen: Week 2 in IDP country: 158 is a crime scene, 322 is a new religion, and a good score is still an L if the other guy prints more. The Host dropped a kitty that made last week’s 315 look like a warm-up — and started Waddle for 27 after last week’s single. Three boards cracked 250 and still lost: Slumlords’ 252, Eddies’ 251.5, and Jacob’s Hyper at 272 in a seven-point street fight. Mike Heff’s Goats fed the league a 66-burger from Devin Lloyd. Luke stayed undefeated. The dual-era champ and the Dongers both woke up 0-2. Hero of the week: Pocket Agents at 322.5 (Goff 43 / CeeDee 41 / Will Anderson 39) and Lloyd’s 66. Goat of the week: Dongers’ 158.5, and a format that turns 250 into heartbreak three times in one Tuesday.
heroes: Pocket Agents 322.5 — Goff 43 / CeeDee 41 / Will Anderson 39; Waddle 27 revenge; week kitty
Devin Lloyd 66 (Goats) — IDP nuclear in a 274.5 over Eddies
Davante Adams 47 (Newman) — from a Week 1 five to a beatdown of Doubtpfizer
Ultron’s first W — Hooker 30 / Cook 29 / Chase 26 after the W1 garage sale
goats: Dongers 158.5 — league floor; Goedert 1.5 on the other sideline still a W for TTAB
Quality-loss club — Slumlords 252, Eddies 251.5, Hyper 272 (all real boards, all Ls)
Doubtpfizer 213 — dual champ at 0-2 despite Dak 37 / Dean 32
LAB offense — Atwell 2; Davis-Gaither’s 32 carried a funeral to 182
Herbert 9 / TLaw 4 / Maye 6 — QB tax across three otherwise grown-up cards

matchups.blurb: The Host did not ask for a second chance — he ordered a nuclear stack. Kellen Olson’s Pocket Agents dropped a **322.5** kitty built on **Jared Goff (43), CeeDee Lamb (41), and Will Anderson Jr. (39)**, then twisted the knife with the punchline of the week: **Jaylen Waddle scored 27** after last week’s flex single. Add **Dalton Kincaid 28** and **Trey McBride 23.5** and you’ve got a TE room that could bully half the league by itself. Ryan Towner’s Slumlords — already Survivor Week 1 alumni — still posted a very real **252**. **Dalton Schultz 41** and **Budda Baker 38** showed up; **Drake Maye managed 6** and London stayed quiet-adjacent at **11**. In any other matchup that 252 buys you a win column. Against 322.5 it’s a footnote with a pulse — the same cruel math that also ate Eddies’ 251.5 and Hyper’s 272. Juice: 322.5; the Goff/CeeDee/Anderson triad; Waddle’s redemption arc. Junk: Maye’s 6; a 252 that wins most weeks and still looks like heartbreak.

matchups.scoreline: Valley Old Goats 274.5, Eagle Ridge Eddies 251.5
matchups.blurb: Heff’s Goats closed **274.5** behind a headline that needs no adjective: **Devin Lloyd dropped 66**. Sixty-six. On IDP. **Patrick Mahomes added 40** while **T.J. Watt (21)** kept the defense honest. Bill’s Eddies put up a real **251.5** — an IDP choir of **Evan Williams 34, Quentin Lake 28, Leonard Williams 27, Dorian Williams 27** — and still left empty-handed, with **Trevor Lawrence’s ceremonial 4** as the sour note on an otherwise grown-up card. Same movie as Slumlords and Hyper this week: you scored enough to win most matchups and still took the L. Juice: Lloyd’s 66; Mahomes’ 40; Goats to 2-0. Junk: TLaw’s 4; another 250+ that tastes like a loss.

Seven points. Rookie franchise vs the commissioner. Luke’s Saltese stayed **2-0** at **279**, powered by **Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s 54**, with **Matthew Stafford (40), DeVonta Smith (35), and Edgerrin Cooper (35)** stacking the rest of the crime. Jacob Crisp’s Hyper put up a very grown-up **272** — **Amon-Ra St. Brown 41, Kenneth Walker 32**, plus a **Nick Bolton / Blake Cashman 30–30** IDP tandem — and still walked away empty because **Justin Herbert managed 9**. That’s the week’s thesis in one box: 272 is a win most Tuesdays, and this Tuesday it joined Slumlords’ 252 and Eddies’ 251.5 in the quality-loss club. Jacob’s Week 1 Monday heist met Week 2’s reality check. Juice: JSN’s 54; Luke undefeated. Junk: Herbert’s 9; 272 as a losing number; the seven-point scar.

matchups.scoreline: Newman Lake Sleep Paralysis Demons 261, Mrs. Doubtpfizer 213
matchups.blurb: Rymo remembered how WR1s are supposed to work. After **Davante Adams’ Week 1 five-spot**, Newman printed **261** with **Adams’ 47** and **Jonathan Taylor’s 32**, plus **Azeez Al-Shaair’s 25** on IDP for the encore. Kyle Weberg’s dual-era champ landed at **213** — **Dak Prescott 37** and **Nakobe Dean 32** were real punches, **CMC 23** was fine — and it’s still **0-2**. Not a Dongers-zone collapse. Just ugly for a franchise that usually loses cute. Juice: Adams’ revenge 47; JT’s 32; Newman back to .500. Junk: champ résumé, 0-2 reality.

Tim’s Divers went to **2-0** the unspectacular way: **215** over Nate’s Substation **171**. **Travis Kelce (39)** did adult TE things while **Bobby Okereke (28)** and **Byron Young (23)** handled the IDP math — even with **Justin Jefferson at 8** and **Deebo at 8** ghosting the skill board. Substation got **Brock Purdy’s 32** and still could not drag **Alec Pierce (2)** and **David Montgomery (4)** across the line. After Week 1’s statement, Morningside just collected. Juice: Divers quietly perfect; Kelce’s 39. Junk: Pierce’s 2; Monty’s 4; Sub’s 171.

Chase’s TTAB stayed **2-0** without needing another 315 — just **Josh Allen’s 47**, **Dee Winters’ 26**, and **Caleb Downs’ 22** clearing a very low bar, even with **Dallas Goedert’s 1.5** as the trade hangover punchline. Gavin’s Dongers bottomed the league at **158.5**. **Kyle Hamilton (32), Bijan (24), and Olave (22)** showed up; the rest of the board did not. After blowing a Week 1 lead on Monday, Week 2 was a flatline. Allen alone outscored the vibe. Juice: TTAB 2-0 on Allen and IDP. Junk: 158.5 league floor; Goedert’s 1.5; Dongers 0-2 with nothing cute about it.

Aga’s first Wheels Up win of 2026, and it was an IDP heist. Ultron’s offense managed **78.5** — **Caleb Williams 6**, **Loveland 1.5**, **Quentin Johnston 1** — while the defense printed **122** and **Amani Hooker (30)** headlined the rescue. **James Cook (29)** and **Ja’Marr Chase (26)** finally showed up after the Week 1 garage-sale tape. Jesse’s LAB hit **182** with **Akeem Davis-Gaither’s 32** and **Quay Walker’s 23** carrying an offense that featured **Tutu Atwell for 2**. That’s a win for Ultron’s identity and a warning label for LAB’s skill slots. Juice: Hooker’s 30; Cook/Chase bounce-back; Aga to 1-1. Junk: Caleb’s 6; Atwell’s 2; winning ugly on defense.

recaps.closer: Kitty to Pocket. League floor to Dongers. Three teams cracked 250 and still lost — Slumlords 252, Eddies 251.5, Hyper 272. Luke 2-0 by seven. Heff’s Lloyd dropped 66. Adams remembered how to WR1. Waddle scored 27. Aga finally cashed a W on Hooker’s IDP. WWJDD: start your studs, fear linebackers named Lloyd, and don’t confuse a 250 with a win.

recaps.title: Week 1 Recap: TTAB Hits the Lottery, Jacob’s First Win, Slumlords Get Off the Bus
recaps.dateLabel: Tuesday drop · Week 1 finals locked after MNF
recaps.coldOpen: Welcome back to IDP country, where 220 is a Tuesday, 315 is a war crime, and Monday night still flips scoreboards like a light switch. Week 1’s thesis was simple: premium draft capital does not equal points, Fantrax IDP math is a rumor, and the only board that mattered was the one still alive after Monday. We got a kitty jackpot, a Survivor eviction, Jacob Crisp’s first Wheels Up win, and enough goose eggs from “safe” stars to stock a diner. Hero of the week: whoever waited until after MNF to write the recap — and T.J. Watt’s 52. Goat of the week: Fantrax projections, Aga’s top-3, and the Host’s Waddle flex.
heroes: TTAB’s 315 — Allen 45 / Watson 44 / Jeanty 41 / Baun 35; kitty locked
Jacob Crisp’s first WU win — Hyper 259.5 over Dongers 246.5 (Monday heist; Walker 48)
T.J. Watt 52 (Goats) — half-century IDP and a 254 close
Gesicki 23 (Saltese) — no-name TE beat Bill’s premium room
goats: Slumlords 176.5 — Survivor Week 1; London 4 / Pickens 5 / Fannin 5; off the bus
Aga’s top-3 (Ultron) — Chase 3 / Cook 10 / Loveland 0 (plus Garrett 0)
Eddies’ TE tax — Gesicki 23 vs Warren 12 + Pitts 0
The Host’s Waddle — started flex, scored 1
Dongers 246.5 — lost a game they thought they’d already won

matchups.blurb: Chase didn’t win Week 1 so much as commit a hate crime against the format. While half the league was still arguing about projections, TTAB put **Josh Allen (45), Christian Watson (44), Ashton Jeanty (41), and Zack Baun (35)** on the same card and printed a **315** kitty that made 250 look quaint. That’s not a hot streak — that’s four players who would’ve been a respectable team by themselves wearing one jersey. Ryan Towner’s Slumlords climbed from the early wreckage to **176.5** after Monday and still finished dead last: Gibbs’ **42** was a lighthouse in a fog of **Drake London 4, George Pickens 5, and Harold Fannin 5**. Survivor doesn’t care that you “fought back.” Off the bus. Juice: the nuclear four and a league-high water mark. Junk: a Gibbs 42 in a funeral; London/Pickens/Fannin quiet hours.

Bill brought **241** to a gunfight and still left with an L — and the TE board was a personal foul. Luke’s Saltese closed it **255–241**, fourteen points that will live rent-free next to the “all-time wins, zero rings” plaque. The humiliation wasn’t even the margin; it was the position battle. Luke started **Mike Gesicki for 23**. Bill started his high-draft-capital room and got **Tyler Warren 12** plus **Kyle Pitts 0** in the flex, with Brock Bowers riding pine for another zero. Gesicki alone outscored Warren and smoked the combined Warren+Pitts stack **23–12** — a no-name TE winning the week against a “premium” room. That’s how you go 0-1 with a roster that was supposed to bully people at the position. Juice: Saltese finishing the job; Gesicki’s 23. Junk: Bill’s TE tax, Pitts’ zero, 241 as a losing score.

Tim’s Divers dropped a clean **258.5** and reminded the dual-era champ that Week 1 doesn’t care about your résumé. The engine was the **Swift / Lamar / JJ** stack doing adult work while the rest of the board finished the job Monday made honest. Kyle’s Doubtpfizer landed at **237** — not a collapse into oblivion, just ugly-adjacent for a franchise that usually loses cute. And then there’s the chip you don’t cash: **Brian Burns started for 4**, which is not how “safe” DL is supposed to look on a losing card. Divers win, doubt deferred. Juice: Divers’ skill stack closing the week. Junk: Burns’ four-point apology.

matchups.scoreline: Valley Old Goats 254, Newman Lake Sleep Paralysis Demons 221
matchups.blurb: Heff’s Goats turned an early knife fight into a **254–221** statement after Monday, and the engine was borderline unfair. **T.J. Watt dropped 52** — a half-century on IDP — while **Derrick Henry stamped 43** like the ground still owed him money. Rymo’s Newman answered with real juice from Flowers and Hurts, then watched the alphas ghost the assignment: **A.J. Brown 5** and **Davante Adams 5** as starters. That’s ten combined from two WR1s while Watt alone outscored both of them by a career. 221 is a fine score in most leagues. Here it’s a handshake and a ‘tough one.’ Juice: Watt’s 52 and Henry’s 43. Junk: Brown + Adams totaling a single good TE game.

Jesse’s LAB posted **246** and made it look like a plan. Kellen “the Host” Olson’s Pocket finished **216.5** after selling Bo Nix for $10 FAAB and handing Goff the keys — a transaction that already had the group chat warming up. Then Monday delivered the roast that writes itself: **Jaylen Waddle started in the flex for 1 point.** One. The Host’s featured WR put up a single on fantasy TV and the board still had the nerve to look surprised at 216.5. Hosting duties that didn’t include actual receiving yards. Juice: LAB’s 246. Junk: Waddle’s 1; the Nix-for-FAAB hangover.

THE flip — and **Jacob Crisp’s first Wheels Up victory**. Rookie season, Week 1, Monday night heist: Hyper went from a **202.5** loss to a **259.5** win and stole Gavin’s board while the league was already writing Dongers’ win tweet. **Kenneth Walker III dropped 48** as the lead actor while the rest of the Hyper lineup finally showed up for the new franchise’s first column in the W. Dongers still hit **246.5** with Bijan and Olave at **34** each — a perfectly respectable losing score in this format’s cruel new math — and somehow lost a game they thought they’d already won. First wins don’t come prettier than a Monday erasure. Juice: Jacob’s first W; Walker’s 48; the 57-point Monday swing. Junk: 246.5 tasting like a losing score.

Nate’s Substation closed **193–180** after buying Bo Nix for $10 FAAB (still shopping Purdy, McLaurin, and Tuten on the block) — and **Nix started for 5** in his new colors, which is comedy enough before you even open Ultron’s card. Aga’s Ultron is the garage-sale roast Bill ordered: top-shelf draft capital, empty shelves, lonely QB heroics. **Ja’Marr Chase 3, James Cook 10, and Colston Loveland 0** hit the field as starters, then **Myles Garrett added a 0** on DL for the encore. That’s Aga’s top-3 totaling **13** while Caleb Williams’ **41** tried to drag a brick wall across the finish line. Sub gets over the hump; Ultron gets the tape. Juice: Substation getting the W. Junk: Chase/Cook/Loveland totaling 13; Garrett’s zero.

recaps.closer: Kitty to TTAB. Bus seat vacated by Slumlords. Jacob Crisp cashed his first WU win on Monday’s Hyper heist. Bill’s 0-1 with a 241 and a TE room that lost to Gesicki. Aga’s top-3 totaled 13. The Host started Waddle for a single. WWJDD: start your studs, ignore Fantrax IDP math, and don’t celebrate until the Monday board is empty.
